rationale: `_Cultist` (cultists.py:14-42) is a SIM-ONLY intermediate base with no C# counterpart. The roster resolves monster/__cultist to src/Core/Models/Monsters/Cultist.cs, which does not exist: the game ships TWO unrelated `public sealed class ... : MonsterModel` files, CalcifiedCultist.cs and DampCultist.cs, each carrying its OWN full copy of GenerateMoveStateMachine, IncantationMove, DarkStrikeMove and the SFX accumulator. There is no shared cultist base type anywhere in src/Core/Models/Monsters/ - the duplication is the source's own. The sim factors the identical half out; the factoring is not observable, because the two concrete subclasses build byte-identical graphs to their own C# models (audited in monster/calcified_cultist and monster/damp_cultist, both faithful on GenerateMoveStateMachine). Executed with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py cultist-base`: `_Cultist(hooks, rng)` raises AttributeError: '_Cultist' object has no attribute 'dark_strike_dmg' (the class declares dark_strike_dmg/incantation_amt as bare annotations, cultists.py:18-19, and defines no values - `_Cultist class attrs with values: {}`), so the base is abstract in practice and can never enter a combat on its own. Recorded as sim_only rather than pointed at one of the two C# files because pointing it at either would make the record claim a 1:1 mapping that does not exist and would double-count that file's overrides. REPORTED, NOT APPLIED (the relic stream owns name_overrides.json): the entry that would silence the roster's UNMATCHED line is {"monster": {"__cultist": null}} if the file supports an explicit sim-only marker, otherwise the roster should keep reporting it and this record is the answer.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: The one behaviour the base owns. It builds INCANTATION_MOVE (BUFF) -> DARK_STRIKE_MOVE (ATTACK, self.dark_strike_dmg) -> itself, initial state INCANTATION_MOVE, states [INCANTATION, DARK_STRIKE] - which is exactly CalcifiedCultist.cs:66-75 and DampCultist.cs:66-75, both of which spell the same graph out separately. Executed (monster_probes_b03.py cultist-base): both subclasses report states ['DARK_STRIKE_MOVE','INCANTATION_MOVE'], kinds ['MoveState'], RandomBranchState count=0, initial=INCANTATION_MOVE, state_log=['INCANTATION_MOVE'].

__init__.rationale: Only supplies the rng default and calls super(). It applies no power, reads no combat state and touches no list that does not exist yet, so SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's escalation clause does not apply.

The build failure is also explained: the constructor argument is not the blocker - `_Cultist(hooks, rng)` still raises AttributeError on the unset dark_strike_dmg class annotation, because the intent is built from it inside build_machine.
